body:
I wrote this code by hand. However, I am not sure about the correct pattern to delete an element from a HashMap while iterating it. Skimming `hash_map.h` I believed it would be unsafe to just drop `transition_map.erase(K.key)` into the existing loop because the `for (... &K: transition_map)` syntax would use an iterator behind the scenes, and that erasing the key invalidates the HashMapElement stored within the iterator.

[**AI assistance disclosure**](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#ai-assisted-contributions): I used Claude to check my belief that the simple `erase()` call would be unsafe, analysing `hash_map.h` for reference. It agreed.

I'm still not 100% sure on this point though. Searching the codebase the old-fashioned way finds some examples of the "advance iterator before removing the current element" pattern that I used, such as:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/bfbe95e510a82f8db6e56220b268ca5945b726fd/editor/debugger/editor_performance_profiler.cpp#L311-L322

(I reused the variable names `E` and `N` from this loop.)

~~However there are also examples that do not use this pattern, e.g. `SceneTreeEditor::NodeCache::delete_pending`:~~

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/bfbe95e510a82f8db6e56220b268ca5945b726fd/editor/scene/scene_tree_editor.cpp#L2543-L2569

~~Here, on line 2544 `I` is initialised with `to_delete.begin()`. Then on line 2552, `to_delete.remove(I)`. Finally on line 2568, `++I`. Is this safe? I think it isn't, but I would appreciate a human's opinion. If it is safe, I can simplify the patch here a lot.~~ *Edit*: On closer inspection, this is a `HashSet` not a `HashMap` being iterated, so whether or not it is safe is irrelevant to my question. Every instance I can find in the codebase of iterating a HashMap does indeed advance the iterator before removing the current element.
